sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Introduces the Bi-Regional Workshop on National Health Accounts held in New Delhi (28 November–1 December 2006) for 26 participants from eight South-East Asia and three Western Pacific countries to strengthen national health financial management through technical training and cross-country learning.

sections.extract: Introduction A Bi-Regional Workshop on National Health Accounts (NHA) was held in New Delhi from 28 November to 1 December 2006. This was a multi- country Activity (MCA) for the countries of the SEA Region; the initiative for which was taken by India with support from the Regional Offices. sections.title: National Health Accounts: A tool for understanding health system financing and equity

summary.text: Summarizes Professor Peter Berman’s two-part presentation on National Health Accounts as a descriptive tool for analyzing health system financing and equity, covering key policy questions, technical boundaries, institutional placement, sustainability, and four best-practice guidelines.

sections.extract: National Health Accounts: A tool for understanding health system financing and equity In Part I of his presentation Professor Peter Berman, (Lead Economist with the World Bank, New Delhi) placed NHA in the context health systems and health financing. sections.title: National Health Accounts: Estimating expenditure

summary.text: Outlines the five-part technical session on estimating public, out-of-pocket, health insurance, private firm and NGO, and external flow health expenditures, including definitions, data sources, estimation methods, and regional country examples.

sections.extract: National Health Accounts: Estimating expenditure This session was divided into five presentations, each of which covered a key area of health expenditure: (1) Estimating public health expenditures. (2) Estimating out-of-pocket expenditures. (3) Understanding health insurance in the NHA framework. sections.title: NHA and data requirement issue

summary.text: Lists the learning objectives of the session on National Health Accounts data requirements, covering data collection planning, data accuracy and relevance, secondary data sources, and primary survey instrument design.

sections.extract: NHA and data requirement issue This session involved with on data requirement issues of NHA, with the following learning objectives: (1) Recommended steps for organizing the data collection process, including the data plan. sections.title: NHA: Boundaries and classification of health expenditure

summary.text: States the learning objectives for the session on National Health Accounts boundaries and classification, focusing on space and time boundaries, the International Classification for Health Accounts (ICHA) coding system, and introducing nationally relevant categories.

sections.extract: NHA: Boundaries and classification of health expenditure This session was aimed at providing and understanding the boundaries and classification of health expenditure in the NHA process. Accordingly, the learning objectives were: (1) Familiarity with the space and time boundaries for health expenditures. sections.title: Susmania case study

summary.text: Describes the three-part group exercise using a fictional country case study (“Susmania”) to give participants practical experience in selecting information from questionnaires and populating National Health Accounts tables.

sections.extract: Susmania case study A case study based on data from a fictional country ‘Susmania’ was conducted in order to: (1) Gain practical experience in filling NHA tables. (2) Be able to select relevant information from NHA questionnaires. sections.title: Country presentations

summary.text: Synthesizes country presentations on planning and institutionalizing National Health Accounts, highlighting lessons shared by India and Thailand on creating policy-maker demand, locating NHA teams effectively, and standardizing public and private sector data collection.

sections.extract: This session was organised to exchange experiences in setting up the NHA process in countries. sections.title: Overview of NHA sub-accounts

summary.text: Introduces National Health Accounts sub-accounts for tracking disaggregated expenditures by specific disease, intervention cluster, age group, or region within the general NHA framework, illustrated by Thailand’s National AIDS Spending Assessment (NASA).

sections.extract: Overview of NHA sub-accounts The purpose of this section of the workshop was to provide an introduction to advancements in the use of NHA. sections.title: Taking the NHA agenda forward in countries of the SEA Region

summary.text: Outlines WHO SEARO’s commitment to advancing the National Health Accounts agenda across the South-East Asia Region by adapting the global curriculum, building a core network of regional resource persons, and providing follow-up country support to institutionalize NHA and link evidence to policy.

sections.extract: of the SEA Region WHO SEARO is committed to pushing the NHA agenda forward in the South East Asia Region. The workshop was an important step in this direction and contributed to the development of a critical mass for NHA development and advocacy in countries. sections.title: Concluding remarks

summary.text: Records the concluding remarks by Dr Anton Fric, who reaffirmed National Health Accounts as a vital policy tool for health systems development and assured participants of continued WHO Regional Office support.

sections.extract: Concluding remarks Dr Anton Fric made the closing remarks by reiterating the fact that the NHA is an important policy tool for health systems development and expressed the hope that participants are convinced that NHA is possible and that they would take the initiative to advocate for it in their countries.
